title: Inverse-eigenvector product conjecture for Gram matrices
statement:
Let $M$ be a real $n\times n$ Gram matrix with diagonal entries equal to $1$. A vector $\alpha=(\alpha_i)_{i=1}^n$ is an **inverse eigenvector** of $M$ if

$$
M\alpha=\alpha^{-1},\qquad \alpha^{-1}=\left(\frac1{\alpha_1},\dots,\frac1{\alpha_n}\right).
$$

**Inverse-eigenvector product conjecture.** There exists an inverse eigenvector $\alpha$ such that

$$
\left|\prod_{i=1}^n\alpha_i\right|\leqslant1.
$$

The source states that this linear-algebraic formulation implies the original real polarization problem. The existence assertion is left as a conjecture.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.05379

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).
source_name: Gergely Ambrus, “Analytic and Probabilistic Problems in Discrete Geometry”, arXiv:1907.05379 (2019).
